Done. All 12 tests in `dominoes_test.go` pass, `go vet` is clean, and the benchmark runs at ~2.5µs/op. No files were created and `dominoes_test.go` was untouched.

The implementation in `dominoes.go`:

- **`type Domino [2]int`** — the stone type the tests expect (`{1, 2}` literals, array comparison).
- **`MakeChain`** — 
  - Empty input → `([]Domino{}, true)`.
  - Quick necessary-condition check: in a *closed* chain every value must appear an even number of times across all halves, so any odd count returns `nil, false` immediately (prunes the "can't be chained" case).
  - Otherwise a backtracking search: try each stone as the first (in both orientations, deduped for doubles), then `build` extends the chain with unused stones whose left half matches the current tail, trying each in both orientations.
- **`build`** — recursive extension; when all stones are placed it accepts the chain only if the first and last values match.

The search is complete because any valid closed chain can be rotated to start with any of its stones, and flipping+reversing a closed chain yields another closed chain — so trying every stone in both orientations as the first covers all solutions. This handles the tricky cases: the "need backtrack" case (a greedy path dead-ends, so backtracking finds the real chain), the disconnected cases (even degrees but no single cycle — the search correctly fails), and duplicate stones (each input element is tracked by index).
